```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(knitr)
library(scales)

options(scipen = 999)

case31 <- read_sav("case31-data.sav")

fmt_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
}

one_sample <- function(x, mu) {
  test <- t.test(x, mu = mu)
  tibble(
    n = sum(!is.na(x)),
    mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    t = unname(test$statistic),
    df = unname(test$parameter),
    p = test$p.value
  )
}

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#173f5f", size = 18),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#52697a", size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(color = "#294c60"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_blank()
    )
)

service_names <- c(
  q13r = "Regular share account",
  q14r = "Special subaccounts",
  q15r = "Christmas club account",
  q16r = "Individual retirement account",
  q17r = "MasterCard credit card",
  q18r = "Signature loans",
  q19r = "New car loans",
  q20r = "Late model car loans",
  q21r = "Older model car loans",
  q22r = "Household goods/appliance loans",
  q23r = "Recreational loans",
  q24r = "Share collateralized loans",
  q25r = "IRA loans",
  q26r = "Line of credit loans"
)

awareness_long <- case31 |>
  select(all_of(names(service_names))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "level") |>
  mutate(
    service = unname(service_names[variable]),
    awareness = factor(
      level,
      levels = 1:3,
      labels = c("Unaware", "Aware, not used", "Aware and used")
    )
  )

awareness_summary <- awareness_long |>
  count(service, awareness, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(service) |>
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

awareness_tests <- awareness_long |>
  count(service, awareness, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(service) |>
  summarise(
    test = list(chisq.test(n, p = rep(1 / 3, 3))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(tidy = map(test, broom::tidy)) |>
  unnest(tidy)
```

# Case 31 Research Questions {.smaller}

Employees Federal Credit Union wanted to understand why members use the credit union, why they borrow elsewhere, how aware they are of available services, and how they evaluate operations.

::: small
-   **R1:** Why do people join the Credit Union?
-   **R2:** Why do members use other financial institutions when they need to borrow funds?
-   **R5:** How well are members aware of the services offered by the Credit Union?
-   **R6:** What are members' attitudes and beliefs about how effectively the Credit Union is operated?
:::

# Research design and sample {.smaller .compact}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="52%"}
-   Mail survey of current EFCU members
-   Simple random sample drawn from 3,531 members
-   300 members selected for the original survey
-   Analysis file contains **`r nrow(case31)` respondents**
-   Structured questions with Likert-type and categorical response scales
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3.2
#| fig-align: center

case31 |>
  count(residence = haven::as_factor(q38)) |>
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = percent, fill = residence)) +
  geom_col(width = .7) +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(percent, accuracy = .1)),
            position = position_stack(vjust = .5), color = "white", size = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#173f5f", "#5fa8a8")) +
  labs(title = "Member residence", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
```
:::
:::::

# Analysis plan {.smaller .compact}

| Research question | Measures | Scale | Descriptive analysis | Inferential analysis |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| R1 | Q7 savings rates | 5-point | Frequencies, mean | One-sample t-test vs. 3 |
| R2 | Q8 borrowing rates; Q30 CU rates lower | 5-point | Frequencies, means | One-sample t-tests vs. 3 |
| R5 | Q13-Q26 service awareness | 3 categories | Counts and percentages | Chi-square goodness-of-fit |
| R6 | Q9-Q12; Q31-Q34; Q37 | Mixed | Frequencies, percentages, means | Chi-square and one-sample t-tests |

<p class="stat-note">

Descriptive patterns guide the interpretation. Test statistics appear only as supporting evidence.

</p>

# R1 Savings rates are viewed as average {.smaller .compact}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center

r1_plot <- case31 |>
  filter(!is.na(q7r)) |>
  mutate(rating = factor(q7r, levels = 1:5,
                         labels = c("Very low", "Low", "Average", "High", "Very high"))) |>
  count(rating) |>
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n))

ggplot(r1_plot, aes(rating, percent)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3c6e71", width = .72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(percent, accuracy = 1)), vjust = -.35, size = 5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, .75)) +
  labs(
    title = "Nearly two-thirds selected Average",
    x = "Opinion of savings rates",
    y = "Valid responses"
  )
```

```{r}
#| include: false
r1_test <- one_sample(case31$q7r, 3)
```

<p class="key-result">

Members do not view the savings rate as meaningfully different from average.

</p>

<p class="stat-note">

M = `r sprintf("%.2f", r1_test$mean)`, SD = `r sprintf("%.2f", r1_test$sd)`; t(`r r1_test$df`) = `r sprintf("%.2f", r1_test$t)`, p `r fmt_p(r1_test$p)`.

</p>

# R2 Borrowing rates do not provide a clear advantage {.smaller .compact}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-align: center

r2_long <- bind_rows(
  case31 |> transmute(
    measure = "Rates charged on borrowed funds (Q8)",
    response = factor(q8r, levels = 1:5,
                      labels = c("Very low", "Low", "Average", "High", "Very high"))
  ),
  case31 |> transmute(
    measure = "CU loan rates are lower (Q30)",
    response = factor(q30, levels = 1:5,
                      labels = c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Uncertain", "Agree", "Strongly agree"))
  )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(response)) |>
  count(measure, response) |>
  group_by(measure) |>
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(r2_long, aes(response, percent, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, width = .72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(percent, accuracy = 1)), vjust = -.25, size = 3.8) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, .58)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#173f5f", "#5fa8a8")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Valid responses") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 24, hjust = 1, size = 10))
```

# R2 Interpretation {.smaller .compact}

```{r}
#| include: false
r2_q8 <- one_sample(case31$q8r, 3)
r2_q30 <- one_sample(case31$q30, 3)

r2_table <- tibble(
  Measure = c("Q8: borrowing rates", "Q30: CU rates lower"),
  `Valid n` = c(r2_q8$n, r2_q30$n),
  Mean = sprintf("%.2f", c(r2_q8$mean, r2_q30$mean)),
  SD = sprintf("%.2f", c(r2_q8$sd, r2_q30$sd)),
  Test = c(
    sprintf("t(%d) = %.2f, p %s", r2_q8$df, r2_q8$t, fmt_p(r2_q8$p)),
    sprintf("t(%d) = %.2f, p %s", r2_q30$df, r2_q30$t, fmt_p(r2_q30$p))
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
kable(r2_table, align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "l"))
```

<p class="key-result">

Members see borrowing rates as approximately average and do not clearly agree that EFCU offers lower rates than competitors.

</p>

<p class="small">

This weak perceived rate advantage helps explain why some members borrow from other financial institutions.

</p>

# R5 Awareness varies sharply by service {.smaller .compact}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.2
#| fig-align: center

service_order <- awareness_summary |>
  filter(awareness == "Unaware") |>
  arrange(percent) |>
  pull(service)

awareness_summary |>
  mutate(service = factor(service, levels = service_order)) |>
  ggplot(aes(service, percent, fill = awareness)) +
  geom_col(width = .72) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .01))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#bd5d5d", "#e5b567", "#3c6e71")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Respondents", fill = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10.5))
```

# R5 Interpretation {.smaller .compact}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false

r5_highlights <- tibble(
  Finding = c(
    "Highest unawareness",
    "Highest reported use",
    "Strong awareness, limited use",
    "Services needing attention"
  ),
  Result = c(
    "Regular share account: 64.8% unaware",
    "MasterCard credit card: 43.8% used",
    "Signature loans: 81.2% aware but not used",
    "IRA loans and share-collateralized loans"
  )
)

kable(r5_highlights, align = c("l", "l"))
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
<p class="key-result">

Awareness patterns differed across all services.

</p>

<p class="small">

All fourteen chi-square goodness-of-fit tests were significant at p \< .001. Responses were concentrated in particular awareness levels.

</p>

<p class="small">

Priority: promote high-unawareness services and examine why loan awareness does not translate into use.

</p>
:::
:::::

# R6 Account communication is mostly effective {.smaller .compact}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-align: center

q9_plot <- case31 |>
  mutate(response = factor(q9r, levels = 1:5,
                           labels = c("Never", "Not often enough", "About right", "Very often", "Too often"))) |>
  count(response, .drop = FALSE) |>
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n), measure = "Statement frequency")

q10_plot <- case31 |>
  mutate(response = factor(q10r, levels = 1:4,
                           labels = c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Excellent"))) |>
  count(response, .drop = FALSE) |>
  mutate(percent = n / sum(n), measure = "Statement accuracy")

bind_rows(q9_plot, q10_plot) |>
  ggplot(aes(response, percent, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, width = .72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(percent, accuracy = 1)), vjust = -.25, size = 4.2) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, .85)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#173f5f", "#5fa8a8")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Respondents") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

<p class="small">

77.3% receive statements about as often as they want, while 22.7% say statements are not frequent enough. Accuracy ratings are strongly favorable: 95.3% selected Good or Excellent.

</p>

# R6 Confidentiality and service delivery {.smaller .compact}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center

binary_summary <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    measure = "Statements easy to understand",
    favorable = mean(case31$q11 == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  tibble(
    measure = "Account information kept confidential",
    favorable = mean(case31$q12[case31$q12 %in% 1:2] == 1)
  )
)

ggplot(binary_summary, aes(reorder(measure, favorable), favorable)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3c6e71", width = .62) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(favorable, accuracy = .1)), vjust = -.35, size = 5) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1.08)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Favorable response")
```
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false

q11_test <- chisq.test(table(factor(case31$q11, levels = 1:2)), p = c(.5, .5))
q12_valid <- ifelse(case31$q12 %in% 1:2, case31$q12, NA)
q12_test <- chisq.test(table(factor(q12_valid, levels = 1:2)), p = c(.5, .5))
```

<p class="key-result">

Statements are easy to understand, while confidence in confidentiality is less universal.

</p>

<p class="small">

Easy to understand: 97.7% Yes (chi-square(1) = `r sprintf("%.2f", unname(q11_test$statistic))`, p \< .001).

</p>

<p class="small">

Information kept confidential: 69.8% Yes among valid responses (chi-square(1) = `r sprintf("%.2f", unname(q12_test$statistic))`, p \< .001).

</p>
:::
:::::

# R6 Operations receive positive ratings  {.smaller .compact}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-align: center

operations <- tibble(
  item = c(
    "Financial information kept confidential",
    "Prompt loan processing",
    "Services meet members' needs",
    "Loan applications are simple",
    "Overall management and operations"
  ),
  mean = c(
    mean(case31$q31, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(case31$q32, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(case31$q33, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(case31$q34, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(case31$q37r, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

ggplot(operations, aes(mean, reorder(item, mean))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, color = "#bd5d5d", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 3, xend = mean, yend = item), color = "#9eb6c3", linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(color = "#173f5f", size = 5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", mean)), hjust = -0.55, size = 4.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(2.8, 4.35), breaks = seq(3, 4.25, .25)) +
  labs(x = "Mean rating", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11))
```

<p class="stat-note">

Each mean was significantly above the neutral benchmark of 3 (all p \< .001). Overall management and operations received the strongest rating (M = 4.07).

</p>

# Conclusions {.smaller .compact}

::: small
1.  **Savings and borrowing rates lack a clear advantage.** Members rate both near average, and they do not clearly agree that EFCU loan rates are lower than competitors.
2.  **Service awareness is uneven.** Awareness varies greatly by service, and several loan products are known but not used.
3.  **Operational perceptions are favorable.** Members report clear statements, accurate information, prompt service, and positive overall management.
4.  **Communication still has gaps.** About one-quarter want statements more frequently, and confidentiality receives a weaker favorable percentage than statement clarity.
:::
